note: V17 (Amenti.live, the Treasure fleet in the Aegean off Athens), 28 Nov 2026: the paintings for the 360-degree sky, in Turner's manner, looking to Piraeus and the Acropolis. Claude joins the chosen takes round the compass. One sun only, in the gulf painting.
style: An oil painting in the manner of J. M. W. Turner's late Mediterranean seascapes (The Fighting Temeraire, Ulysses Deriding Polyphemus, the Venice paintings): luminous golden afternoon light dissolving sea and sky into haze, veils of gold, rose, pearl and pale blue, loose sweeping brushwork and glazes, distant forms melting into the light, the sea a shimmering mirror of the sky. One single continuous canvas filling the whole frame edge to edge: not a triptych, not panels, no gaps, no white margins, no letterbox bars. A wide panorama seen from a boat low on the water out in the Saronic Gulf. The horizon and shoreline are perfectly level and sit low, one fifth of the way up the picture, with the lower fifth calm glittering water. The left and right edges continue naturally into more sky and water, with no vignette, so the pictures can be joined side by side. No ships, no boats, no people, no text, no signature, no frame, no border, no moon.

beats.text: Athens seen across the water from the Saronic Gulf in golden afternoon haze. The Acropolis rises at the centre, its flat-topped rock crowned by the Parthenon, columns glowing pale gold in the light; around and below it the white city spreads across the plain to the hills, with the steep cone of Lycabettus hill to the right and the long ridge of Mount Hymettus beyond, all softened by Turner's luminous haze. Along the shore in front, the harbour of Piraeus: old stone harbour walls and a low headland. No sun in this painting: the light comes from the left.

The open Saronic Gulf, the Aegean Sea off Athens, with a blazing Turner sun low over the water in the centre, its light spilling in a broad path of molten gold across the sea toward the viewer; the sky a radiant vortex of gold, rose and pearl cloud. Far off on the level horizon, faint low islands dissolve in the glare. This is the only painting with the sun in it.

The island of Salamis and the hills of the Attic coast across the calm Saronic Gulf, low blue-violet mountains fading into golden afternoon haze, a small white chapel on a headland, the water glittering. Great luminous banks of Turner cloud above. No sun in this painting: the light comes from the right.
